steps.label: Pinnately compound
lines: Pinnately compound leaf: the lamina is cut
from the margin up to the midrib, so the
leaflets sit along a common axis called the
steps.why: The incision pattern decides the type: cuts reaching the MIDRIB leave a central axis (rachis) carrying leaflets on both sides, like a feather.
common_mistakes: Calling the leaflets separate leaves. A bud sits in the axil of the whole leaf, never of a leaflet.
steps.memory_tip: Pinna means feather - leaflets in two rows on a central rachis.
steps.margin_note: Definition + 'rachis present' + neem is the complete half.

steps.label: Palmately compound

lines.text: Palmately compound leaf: the incisions run

lines: to the tip of the petiole, so all leaflets
attach at one point. Rachis absent.
steps.why: When the cuts reach the petiole tip there is no axis left - all leaflets share a single attachment point, like fingers from a palm.
common_mistakes: Writing rachis present for palmate. The absence of the rachis IS the difference.
steps.memory_tip: Palm - all fingers from one point; feather - leaflets along a shaft.
steps.margin_note: State 'rachis absent' explicitly - it is the marked contrast.
